deep.reconstruction:
The page is written upside down relative to the scan. Its content is a single technical task: interchanging the order of integration in a double integral and determining the new limits. Read the notation as follows: x*x = x^2, alpha*alpha*p*p = alpha^2 p^2. Riemann first writes the integrand with x^2/(4 alpha^2 p^2) and then abbreviates it to q^2/4, i.e. q = x/(alpha p).

(A) Starting expression (top of page in the upright reading). Riemann writes
  (1/2) theta ∫∫ e^{i lambda (t-z)} dz ds / sqrt(-s^2 + s z - q^2/4).
The region is bounded by the line z = t + s and the curve z = s + q^2/(4s). The square root is real only when s^2 - s z + q^2/4 < 0, i.e.
  r_- < s < r_+, where r_± = (z ± sqrt(z^2 - q^2))/2,
which Riemann writes as z + sqrt(...) > 2s > z - sqrt(...), equivalently (s - z/2)^2 < (z^2 - q^2)/4. This requires z > q. The other condition is 2s > z - t (in this first block the factor 2 seems to belong to a variant; later he uses s > z - t). The admissible s-range is infinity > 2s > x^2/(2 alpha^2 p^2 t), i.e. s > q^2/(4t). That is where the line meets the curve: s + q^2/(4s) = t + s gives s = q^2/(4t).

(B) Corner point of the region. Setting z - 2t + sqrt(z^2 - q^2) = 0, i.e. z - t equals the lower root r_-, and squaring gives -4zt + 4t^2 + q^2 = 0, so z = t + q^2/(4t). Doing the same with z - q^2/(2t) - sqrt(z^2 - q^2) = 0 gives -(q^2/t) z + q^4/(4t^2) + q^2 = 0, again z = t + q^2/(4t). So the line z = t + s crosses the parabola-like boundary s^2 - s z + q^2/4 = 0 at z0 = t + q^2/(4t). The parabola's leftmost point is z = q, s = q/2. Because z0 ≥ q (AM-GM), with equality iff t = q/2, the case split t ≷ q/2 decides whether the crossing lies on the lower branch s = r_- or the upper branch s = r_+.

(C) Chain of equivalences for z > t + q^2/(4t):
  4zt > 4t^2 + q^2
  => z^2 - q^2 > z^2 - 4zt + 4t^2
  => sqrt(z^2 - q^2) > 2t - z
  => 2(z - t) > z - sqrt(z^2 - q^2), i.e. z - t > r_-.
Similarly (q^2/t) z > q^4/(4t^2) + q^2 gives sqrt(z^2 - q^2) > z - q^2/(2t). The marginal remark 'q/2 < t, sqrt(z^2 - q^2) > z - 2t' secures z - t < r_+.

(D) Result of the interchange (case t > q/2), with the inner variable s and the region s > z - t, r_- < s < r_+:
  - for z > t + q^2/(4t): s runs from z - t to r_+;
  - for q < z < t + q^2/(4t): s runs over the whole interval r_- < s < r_+.
In the second case the inner integral is complete. Riemann writes
  u = ∫_{∞}^{t+q^2/(4t)} ∫_{r_+}^{z-t} ... = P + ∫_{q}^{t+q^2/(4t)} ∫_{r_-}^{r_+} e^{i lambda (t-z)} dz ds / sqrt(...),
and the line 'u = pi ∫ ...' records the evaluation of the complete inner integral. [My completion:] ∫_{r_-}^{r_+} ds / sqrt((s - r_-)(r_+ - s)) = pi, so the second term is pi ∫_q^{t+q^2/(4t)} e^{i lambda (t-z)} dz. For the partial range the inner integral is ∫_{z-t}^{r_+} = arccos((z - 2t)/sqrt(z^2 - q^2)).

(E) Case t < q/2 (lower block in the upright reading). Riemann restarts with
  (1/2) theta ∫_{∞}^{t+s} ∫^{s + q^2/(4s)} ...
under the conditions t + s < z < s + q^2/(4s), infinity > z > q^2/(4t), and 4zs > 4s^2 + q^2, i.e. (z^2 - q^2)/4 > (s - z/2)^2. Some fragmentary inequalities follow ('> q^4/(z^2 - q^2)', '2t + q^2/z + sqrt(z^2 - q^2) > 2z'); these are partly illegible and unfinished. Here the crossing lies on the upper branch r_+.

(F) Bottom-right fragments. The boundary is written as (s - z/2)^2 = (z^2 - q^2)/4. There is an expression (1/2) theta ∫ e^{i lambda (t-z)} dz ... sqrt(1 - q^2) ... with the condition 1 < q^2, apparently a normalized (q-scaled) variant.

Purpose (my interpretation, not stated on the page). The structure fits a Fourier-type representation of the solution of a propagation problem with a damping parameter: e^{i lambda (t-z)} combined with an Abel/arcsine kernel 1/sqrt(s(z-s) - q^2/4) and q = x/(alpha p). Such kernels give Bessel-J0-type expressions as in telegraph/cable or heat-conduction problems. Riemann reduces the double integral to single integrals over z with an arccos or a constant pi as kernel. The next page (the Dissertation draft on complex functions) is unrelated.
errors: No mathematical errors in the legible algebra. The squarings in (B) and (C) are correct and both give z = t + q^2/(4t). Squaring 'sqrt(z^2-q^2) > 2t - z' is only legitimate when 2t - z ≥ 0; otherwise the inequality is trivial. Riemann does not comment on this, but the conclusion holds either way.
The first block writes 2s > z - t and 2s > x^2/(2 alpha^2 p^2 t), whereas later blocks use s > z - t and s > q^2/(4t). The factor 2 is inconsistently placed (an early variant or a slip).
Some inequalities in the t < q/2 block ('> q^4/(z^2-q^2)', '2t + q^2/z + sqrt(z^2-q^2) > 2z') are incomplete or uncertain in reading and cannot be verified as written.

results.what: Determination of the new limits when swapping the order of integration over the region bounded by z = t + s and s^2 - s z + q^2/4 = 0, with the corner at z = t + q^2/(4t) and the case split t ≷ q/2
results.modern_name: Fubini/Dirichlet interchange of integration order for a double integral

results.what: Complete inner integral ∫_{r_-}^{r_+} ds / sqrt(-s^2 + s z - q^2/4) = pi, and the partial integral as an arccos

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of integration limits in a double integral, presumably part of Riemann's work on a physical propagation/conduction problem (an integral representation related to Bessel-type kernels). Nothing here goes beyond standard technique, and the physical context is not identified on the page.

transcription_corrections: The page is written upside down. The block printed first in the transcription (with x^2/(4 alpha^2 p^2)) is at the bottom of the scan in its displayed orientation; it is a natural opening only if one reads the page rotated.
In the line for z < t + q^2/(4t) the ordering of the inequality should read (z+sqrt(z^2-q^2))/2 > s > (z-sqrt(z^2-q^2))/2 (full interval between the roots); the transcription reverses it.
The integrand denominator sqrt(-s^2 + s z - x^2/(4 alpha^2 p^2)) is consistent with q^2 = x^2/(alpha^2 p^2), i.e. q = x/(alpha p).
'u = pi/? ∫' is probably 'u = pi ∫ ...', reflecting the evaluation of the complete inner integral as pi.
The marginal 'st+ss-sz+zz/4 < zz/4' is uncertain. It is more plausibly a rearrangement of s^2 - s z + q^2/4 < 0, e.g. (s - z/2)^2 < (z^2 - q^2)/4.
